Facility: Stanford Medical Center
Original Denial Date: October 25, 2024
Appeal Date: November 8, 2024

Dear Mr. Flores,

HealthFirst has completed its clinical review of the first-level appeal submitted on your behalf by Dr. Karen Davis, MD, regarding the prior authorization denial for a prophylactic anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at the C5-C6 level (CPT 22551). Based on a comprehensive evaluation of your clinical records, the plan's clinical coverage criteria, California regulatory requirements, and generally accepted standards of medical practice, the decision to deny prior authorization has been UPHELD.

I. CLINICAL SUMMARY
The clinical documentation submitted with your request and appeal has been thoroughly reviewed:
- Imaging: A cervical spine MRI dated September 15, 2024, demonstrates severe central canal stenosis at the C5-C6 level with a canal diameter of 6mm (normal is greater than 13mm). The radiologist noted spinal cord contact but explicitly documented "no compression," "no T2 signal change," and "no myelomalacia."
- Clinical Examination: A neurological examination performed on September 20, 2024, was completely normal. There was no evidence of cervical radiculopathy (no dermatomal pain, numbness, or weakness) and no signs of cervical myelopathy (no gait disturbance, no bilateral upper extremity weakness, no hyperreflexia, no positive Hoffman sign, and no upper motor neuron signs). Your primary clinical symptom is axial neck pain, rated at 5/10.
- Conservative Treatment: You have completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 sessions) for axial pain, which resulted in modest pain improvement (from 7/10 to 5/10) but addressed no neurological symptoms. Your pharmacotherapy trial included Naproxen 500mg BID for 3 months (moderate pain relief) and Cyclobenzaprine for 6 weeks (sleep improvement only). You also received a C5-C6 epidural steroid injection on October 10, 2024, which provided 60% pain relief lasting 6 weeks.
- Surgeon's Assessment: Dr. Davis requested prophylactic decompression, noting that your critically narrow canal diameter (6mm) puts you at high risk for acute spinal cord injury from minor trauma, particularly given your occupation as a construction worker operating heavy equipment.

II. PLAN CRITERIA ANALYSIS
Your request was evaluated under the HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria document: Spinal Surgery — Cervical Procedures (CC-SPINE-2024, Effective January 1, 2024).

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1): To qualify for surgical authorization, a member must have a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy (nerve root compression with dermatomal symptoms), cervical myelopathy (spinal cord compression with myelopathic symptoms), or cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit. Your clinical record dated September 20, 2024, explicitly documents a "completely normal neurological examination" with no radiculopathy, no myelopathy, and no upper motor neuron signs. Therefore, you do not meet the diagnostic requirements of Section 2.1.

2. Exclusions (Section 3.1): Section 3.1 explicitly states that authorization will be denied when "surgery is requested solely for axial neck pain without documented radiculopathy or myelopathy." Because your primary clinical complaint is axial neck pain (5/10) and there is no documented radiculopathy or myelopathy, the requested procedure is excluded from coverage under Section 3.1.

III. REGULATORY AND CLINICAL STANDARDS ANALYSIS
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32, the standard of review for medical necessity requires that the requested service be in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice and clinically appropriate for the patient's illness, injury, or disease. CHSC § 1374.32(b) specifies that the plan's internal criteria are not the sole or determinative basis if they are more restrictive than generally accepted standards.

To resolve this, we evaluated your clinical presentation against generally accepted clinical guidelines, including the AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine Guidelines for Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update) and the North American Spine Society (NASS) Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020):
- Tier 3 Classification (Surgery Not Indicated): Under Section 3.1 of the Clinical Reference Summary (derived from AANS/CNS 2023 and NASS 2020 guidelines), surgical intervention is classified as "Tier 3 — Surgery Not Indicated" for "axial neck pain without radiculopathy or myelopathy" (Tier 3(a)) and "imaging findings without correlating symptoms" (Tier 3(b)). Generally accepted standards of medical practice do not support prophylactic surgical decompression (ACDF) for severe cervical stenosis in patients who are completely asymptomatic neurologically and present only with axial neck pain.
- Risk-Benefit Ratio: Clinical evidence indicates that the risks of major spinal surgery (including CPT 22551) outweigh the theoretical benefit of preventing a future traumatic spinal cord injury in an asymptomatic patient, even one in a high-risk occupation. There is no high-quality clinical evidence or guideline supporting prophylactic ACDF based on occupational risk alone.

We also evaluated the Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter APL 22-014, which addresses prior authorization requirements for time-sensitive neurological conditions:
- Under APL 22-014 Part II.1, cervical myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI is classified as an urgent condition where standard conservative treatment requirements may be waived. 
- However, your MRI dated September 15, 2024, explicitly noted "no T2 signal change" and "no myelomalacia," and your clinical exam showed no myelopathy. Therefore, the urgent exceptions under APL 22-014 do not apply to your case.

Because generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020) align with the plan's criteria in excluding surgery for axial pain without neurological deficits, there is no conflict between the plan's criteria and the clinical standard of care. The requested prophylactic surgery does not meet the standard for medical necessity under CHSC § 1374.32.

IV. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS
Because you do not meet the diagnostic requirements of HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.1, are subject to the exclusion in Section 3.1, and do not meet the clinical standard for medical necessity under CHSC § 1374.32 or generally accepted clinical guidelines (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020), the denial of prior authorization is UPHELD.

We recommend that you continue to be monitored closely by your physician for any developing neurological symptoms (such as numbness, tingling, weakness in your arms or legs, or changes in your gait). You should also discuss activity modifications with your physician to mitigate the risk of cervical trauma in your occupation.

V. NOTICE OF INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW (IMR) RIGHTS
Under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.30, you have the right to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) from the Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) if you disagree with this decision. The IMR is an online or paper application process where independent medical specialists review your case. You may submit an application for IMR if the plan's denial has been upheld on appeal. There is no cost to you for this review. You can obtain an IMR application form and instructions by contacting the DMHC Help Center at 1-888-466-2219 or visiting www.dmhc.ca.gov.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Medical Director, HealthFirst Health Plan
Board-Certified Physician Reviewer

# HEALTH PLAN APPEALS & GRIEVANCE DIVISION
**FORMAL APPEAL DETERMINATION**

---

### CASE METADATA
*   **Case ID:** PA-2024-D003
*   **Member Name:** Jessica Turner
*   **Member ID:** M-556688
*   **Plan Type:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
*   **State of Residence:** California (CA)
*   **Plan Year / Coverage Effective:** 2024 / 2023-07-01
*   **Requested Procedure:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, single level (CPT 22551)
*   **Requesting Physician:** Dr. Robert Chen, MD — Spine Surgery
*   **Facility:** Stanford Medical Center
*   **Initial Reviewer:** Dr. Alan Foster, MD (Medical Director)
*   **Initial Denial Date:** October 15, 2024
*   **Reason Code / Written Basis:** MED-003 / Verbal peer-to-peer call only

---

### FINAL DISPOSITION
**OVERTURN** (The initial medical necessity denial is reversed in its entirety on procedural and statutory grounds. The requested single-level ACDF C6-C7 [CPT 22551] is authorized for immediate scheduling.)

---

### SECTION I: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This formal appeal review evaluates the prior authorization denial of an anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 (CPT 22551) requested by Dr. Robert Chen on behalf of Jessica Turner, a 39-year-old California enrollee. 

The initial denial, issued on October 15, 2024, was based solely on a verbal peer-to-peer discussion between the plan's Medical Director, Dr. Alan Foster, and the requesting physician. No written clinical criteria or specific clinical reasons were provided to the member in the denial letter, and the mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice of rights was omitted.

Applying the strict **Hierarchy of Authority** established for this evaluation—where **California State Law and Regulatory Mandates** represent the supreme tier over internal health plan clinical coverage policies—this review finds the plan’s initial denial to be legally and procedurally defective under **California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b)**. Because a procedurally defective denial must be treated as invalid under California law, the denial is **OVERTURNED on procedural grounds**. 

A secondary clinical review confirms that while the member presents with Cervical Radiculopathy rather than Cervical Myelopathy, the mechanical application of the plan's 6-week physical therapy requirement violates **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5**, given the documented functional plateau achieved after 5 weeks (15 sessions) of structured therapy.

---

### SECTION II: EVALUATION PLAN STEP-BY-STEP ANALYSIS

#### 1. Procedural Adequacy Assessment (CHSC § 1374.31(b))
Under California managed care law, health plans must adhere to strict transparency and disclosure requirements when denying prior authorization requests based on medical necessity:
*   **CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2)** explicitly mandates that any denial notice must provide the member and the treating physician with a written statement containing the **specific clinical criteria applied** and the **specific clinical reasons for the denial**, alongside the mandatory **Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice of rights**.
*   **CHSC § 1374.31(b)** dictates that any denial notice failing to specify the clinical criteria or clinical reasons in writing is **procedurally defective** and must be legally treated as if no denial was issued.

*Record Findings for Jessica Turner:*
*   **Written Denial Basis:** "Verbal only — peer-to-peer call" (No written clinical criteria cited).
*   **Specific Clinical Reason Cited in Writing:** None. The denial letter stated: *"Request denied based on peer-to-peer review... Detailed criteria review provided verbally during peer-to-peer call."*
*   **IMR Notice Included:** False (`imr_notice_included: false` and verified as missing).
*   **Criteria Communicated Verbally Only:** True.

*Procedural Determination:*
The plan failed to issue a legally adequate denial notice. Verbal communication during a peer-to-peer call cannot substitute for written, statutory disclosures to the member. Because the plan omitted both the written clinical rationale and the mandatory IMR notice, the denial of October 15, 2024, is **legally defective under CHSC § 1374.31(b)**. 

Pursuant to the **Step 1 Procedural Adequacy Check** of the governing Disposition Decision Tree, a procedural defect requires an immediate **OVERTURN** of the denial.

---

#### 2. Clinical Classification and Pathology Verification (Clinical Standards)
To establish a complete clinical record and address the medical necessity of the underlying request, the clinical documentation was reviewed to classify the patient's pathology as either Cervical Myelopathy or Cervical Radiculopathy. These conditions represent distinct clinical entities with independent therapeutic guidelines (AANS/CNS Guidelines; NASS Guidelines).

*   **Imaging Review (MRI dated 2024-09-01):** Demonstrates a C6-C7 disc herniation resulting in right C7 nerve root compression and moderate foraminal stenosis. Crucially, there is *no* evidence of spinal cord compression, cord signal change, or myelomalacia.
*   **Neurological Examination (2024-09-05):** Reveals right C7 dermatomal numbness and tingling, a diminished right tricep reflex (lower motor neuron sign), and mild grip weakness (4+/5). No upper motor neuron (UMN) signs—such as a positive Hoffman sign, hyperreflexia (clonus), bilateral upper extremity weakness, or gait disturbances—are documented.

*Clinical Classification:*
The member’s clinical and radiographical presentation is diagnostic of **Cervical Radiculopathy (C6-C7)**. There is no clinical or objective radiographical evidence of Cervical Myelopathy. Therefore, standard radiculopathy pathways apply.

---

#### 3. Statutory and Clinical Standard Override Analysis (CIC § 10169.5 & DMHC APL 22-014)
Because the diagnosis is Cervical Radiculopathy without spinal cord compression, the urgent neurological carve-outs for myelomalacia under **DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014** do not apply. 

However, **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5** regulates health insurers' use of physical therapy (PT) as a mandatory prerequisite for surgical authorization:
*   **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)** prohibits a plan from conditioning surgical approval on the completion of physical therapy where the member has completed a course of PT and the treating physician documents that the member reached a **functional plateau** without adequate resolution of symptoms.
*   **CIC § 10169.5(c)** establishes that a plan's internal minimum timeline for physical therapy (such as HealthFirst’s 6-week rule) **shall not be applied mechanically** without considering whether a functional plateau was achieved.

*Conservative Treatment Record Findings:*
*   **Physical Therapy:** The member completed **5 weeks (15 sessions)** of structured PT. The treating physician documented in the appeal letter that the member reached a functional plateau.
*   **Pharmacotherapy:** Complied with a 3-month trial of Meloxicam 15mg daily (NSAID, partial relief) and a 2-week trial of Prednisone taper (Oral corticosteroid, temporary improvement).
*   **Interventional Treatments:** None.

*Override Determination:*
Under HealthFirst's internal criteria (**CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2**), a member must complete 6 weeks of physical therapy. However, the patient completed 5 weeks (15 sessions)—a highly standard clinical duration—and her treating spine surgeon documented a functional plateau. Applying the 6-week clinical criteria mechanically to deny coverage directly violates **CIC § 10169.5(c)**. Under the Hierarchy of Authority, the statutory protections of **CIC § 10169.5** override the plan's 6-week policy limit, legally validating the physical therapy trial.

---

#### 4. Plan Criteria Compliance and Exceptions (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024)
Applying HealthFirst's internal criteria strictly:
*   **Section 2.1 (Diagnosis):** Met. The member has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy supported by an MRI within 6 months showing structural pathology consistent with symptoms (C6-C7 herniation and C7 root compression).
*   **Section 2.2(a) (Physical Therapy):** Unmet under internal guidelines (5 weeks completed vs. 6 weeks required), but overridden by **CIC § 10169.5** as detailed above.
*   **Section 2.2(b) (Pharmacotherapy):** Partially met. The member tried Meloxicam for 3 months (compliant) and Prednisone for 2 weeks (non-compliant with the plan's internal 4-week-per-agent minimum).
*   **Section 2.2(c) (Interventional Treatment):** Unmet (no interventional trials documented).

*Plan Criteria Determination:*
Under a strict, non-statutory reading of the plan's internal guidelines, the request would be denied for failure to complete the 6-week PT course, 4 weeks of a second medication, and an interventional procedure. However, because **State Law (Tier 1)** overrides **Plan Criteria (Tier 3)**:
1.  The procedural failure under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)** legally invalidates the denial itself, requiring an overturn.
2.  The mechanical application of the PT timeline is legally prohibited under **CIC § 10169.5** due to the documented functional plateau.

---

### SECTION III: SUMMARY OF FINDINGS & LEGAL CITATIONS

1.  **Procedural Violation (CHSC § 1374.31):** The plan issued a prior authorization denial without written clinical criteria or specific clinical reasons, relying on verbal peer-to-peer discussions. The plan also failed to issue the mandatory IMR notice of rights. Under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)**, the denial is legally defective and is treated as if no denial was issued.
2.  **Statutory PT Override (CIC § 10169.5):** The patient trialed 5 weeks (15 sessions) of supervised PT and reached a functional plateau documented by her treating physician. Mechanical application of the plan's 6-week PT requirement is legally invalid under **CIC § 10169.5(c)**.
3.  **Hierarchy of Authority Resolution:** The plan's internal clinical policy (**CC-SPINE-2024**) is more restrictive than California statutory mandates (**CHSC § 1374.31** and **CIC § 10169.5**). Therefore, State Law governs. The denial must be overturned on procedural and statutory grounds.

---

### SECTION IV: AUTHORIZATION & INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PLAN

*   **Effective Date of Decision:** Immediate (October 25, 2024)
*   **Approved Procedure:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, single level
*   **CPT Code authorized:** 22551
*   **Provider/Facility authorized:** Dr. Robert Chen, MD / Stanford Medical Center
*   **Authorization Period:** 90 Days from the date of this determination.

**Action Required by Health Plan:**
The health plan is directed to immediately update its claims and prior authorization systems to reflect **Approved** status for CPT code 22551 for member Jessica Turner (M-556688). An official written authorization letter must be issued to the member and Dr. Robert Chen within **2 business days** of this decision, satisfying all notice requirements under California managed care standards.

**HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — APPEAL DETERMINATION**

**CASE ID:** PA-2024-D003
**MEMBER:** Jessica Turner (M-556688)
**PROCEDURE:** ACDF C6-C7, one level (CPT 22551)
**DENIAL DATE:** 2024-10-15
**APPEAL DATE:** 2024-10-18

**APPEAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED**

**WARRANT:**

The denial of prior authorization for Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 for Jessica Turner is **OVERTURNED** for the following reasons, applying the hierarchy of State law > Clinical standard > Plan criteria:

**1. Procedural Defect in Denial Notice (State Law Override)**

The initial denial issued by HealthFirst Plan on 2024-10-15 was procedurally defective, rendering it invalid.
*   **Finding:** The denial was communicated verbally during a peer-to-peer call and explicitly stated "Verbal only — peer-to-peer call" as its basis. The denial also failed to include a notice of Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights.
*   **State Law (CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) & (b)):** California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a)(2) mandates that a denial notice based on medical necessity "Include in the denial notice: the specific criteria applied, the specific clinical reason for the denial, and notice of IMR rights." Furthermore, CHSC § 1374.31(b) states: "A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is DEFECTIVE and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines."
*   **Conclusion:** The denial notice failed to meet multiple statutory requirements, including providing written criteria, specific clinical reasons, and IMR notice. As per CHSC § 1374.31(b), this procedural defect alone renders the denial invalid and requires it to be overturned.

**2. Physical Therapy Requirement Override (State Law Override)**

Even if the denial were procedurally adequate, the plan's denial based on insufficient physical therapy (Plan Criteria 2.2(a) requiring 6 weeks) is overridden by California state law.
*   **Finding:** The member completed 5 weeks of physical therapy (PT), and the treating physician declares a functional plateau in the appeal letter. The MRI dated 2024-09-01 demonstrates "C6-C7 disc herniation, right C7 nerve root compression, moderate foraminal stenosis." The presenting diagnosis is Cervical Radiculopathy C6-C7 with persistent symptoms.
*   **State Law (CIC § 10169.5(a)(2) & (3)):** California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a) explicitly prohibits a health insurer from conditioning approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where:
    *   **(a)(2):** "The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms." The treating physician's declaration of a plateau after 5 weeks of PT meets this criterion.
    *   **(a)(3):** "The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." The MRI findings of C6-C7 disc herniation with right C7 nerve root compression and moderate foraminal stenosis constitute objective structural neurological compromise that PT cannot reverse.
*   **Conclusion:** The plan's 6-week PT requirement is directly overridden by CIC § 10169.5(a)(2) and (3). The 5 weeks of PT completed, combined with the physician-declared plateau and objective structural nerve root compression, are sufficient under California law.

**3. Adequacy of Conservative Treatment (Clinical Standard Override for Restrictive Plan Criteria)**

While the member did not meet all specific components of the plan's conservative treatment criteria (Plan Criteria 2.2(b) for pharmacotherapy and 2.2(c) for interventional treatment), the overall conservative trial, when viewed against generally accepted clinical standards and state law, is deemed adequate.
*   **Finding:** The member completed 5 weeks of PT (accepted per CIC 10169.5), 3 months of Meloxicam (with partial relief), and a 2-week course of Prednisone (with temporary improvement). No interventional procedures were performed. The neurological exam shows persistent right C7 dermatomal numbness and tingling and a diminished tricep reflex, consistent with the MRI findings of C7 nerve root compression.
*   **Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020):** For cervical radiculopathy, surgery is considered a "reasonable option" (AANS/CNS TIER 2) for patients with persistent symptoms after an "adequate conservative trial," often cited as 6-12 weeks of conservative management (NASS Guidelines). The clinical standard does not strictly mandate specific numbers of pharmacotherapy agents or interventional procedures when objective structural pathology and persistent symptoms are present after a trial of conservative care.
*   **State Law (CHSC § 1374.32(b)):** This statute clarifies that the Independent Medical Review standard (which applies to appeals in general) does NOT require adherence to the plan's internal coverage criteria. If the service meets "generally accepted standards of medical practice," it "SHALL be approved regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive."
*   **Conclusion:** With objective nerve root compression, persistent neurological symptoms, and a course of conservative treatment that includes PT (deemed adequate by state law) and a prolonged NSAID trial, the clinical standard supports surgical intervention as a reasonable option. The plan's more stringent requirements for additional pharmacotherapy and an interventional procedure, when a functional plateau has been declared and structural compromise exists, are more restrictive than generally accepted standards of medical practice for this presentation of radiculopathy.

**Overall Conclusion:**

The initial denial is invalid due to significant procedural defects that violate California state law. Furthermore, the plan's basis for denial, likely related to insufficient conservative treatment, particularly physical therapy, is overridden by state statutes and found to be overly restrictive compared to generally accepted clinical standards for cervical radiculopathy with objective nerve root compression and persistent symptoms.

Therefore, the denial is **OVERTURNED**, and authorization for CPT 22551 (ACDF C6-C7, one level) for Jessica Turner is approved.

**Level of Review:** First-Level Appeal

---

**I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

This appeal reviews the denial of a prior authorization request for a two-level ACDF at C5-C6 and C6-C7 for Mr. Victor Patel. The initial denial cited that while C5-C6 demonstrated pathology consistent with surgical criteria, C6-C7 showed only mild changes and did not meet criteria, thus not approving the two-level fusion.

Upon comprehensive review of the clinical record, HealthFirst Plan Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), California regulatory framework (CIC, CHSC, DMHC APL 22-014), and generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021), applying the hierarchy of State Law > Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria, the denial of the **two-level ACDF (C5-C6 and C6-C7) is UPHELD.**

While the C5-C6 level clearly meets medical necessity criteria for surgical intervention, the C6-C7 level does not demonstrate objective evidence of nerve root compression or definitive radiculopathy, failing to meet criteria under both the HealthFirst plan policy and generally accepted clinical standards.

---

**II. CASE BACKGROUND**

Mr. Victor Patel, a 60-year-old member, was diagnosed with two-level cervical disc disease at C5-C6 and C6-C7, with asymmetric severity. Dr. Lisa Park requested prior authorization for a two-level ACDF. The request was denied by HealthFirst, stating C5-C6 met criteria but C6-C7 did not, thus precluding approval for a two-level procedure.

The appeal argues that both levels are symptomatic, adjacent levels should be addressed simultaneously to prevent accelerated degeneration, and the member meets full criteria for both levels.

---

**III. CLINICAL RECORD REVIEW**

1.  **Presenting Diagnosis:** Two-level cervical disc disease C5-C6 and C6-C7 – asymmetric severity.
2.  **Imaging (MRI 2024-09-15):**
    *   **C5-C6:** Large disc herniation, moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression, foraminal stenosis.
    *   **C6-C7:** Small disc bulge, mild foraminal narrowing, **no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact.**
3.  **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):**
    *   **C6 level:** Right bicep weakness 3+/5, bicep reflex absent right, right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling.
    *   **C7 level:** Right tricep reflex slightly diminished. **No definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms.** Physician notes mild C7 symptoms possibly present but not clearly documented.
4.  **Conservative Treatment:**
    *   **Physical Therapy:** 8 weeks, 24 sessions. C6 symptoms persist. **C7 symptoms: minimal and possibly resolving per PT note at week 8.**
    *   **Pharmacotherapy:** Pregabalin 150mg BID (4 months, partial C6 relief, uncertain C7 contribution); Naproxen 500mg BID (3 months, moderate relief).
    *   **Interventional:** Right C6 epidural (2024-10-15), good C6 relief (70%), fully returned in 4 weeks. **No C7-specific injection performed.**

**Crucial Observation:** The clinical record does *not* provide any objective evidence of cervical myelopathy (e.g., spinal cord compression, upper motor neuron signs, gait disturbance, myelomalacia). This case presents as a clear cervical radiculopathy at C5-C6 and, at best, mild and non-objective symptoms at C6-C7.

---

**IV. APPLICATION OF HEALTHFIRST PLAN CRITERIA (CC-SPINE-2024)**

1.  **Denial Adequacy:** The initial denial notice identified the reason (C6-C7 not meeting criteria) and cited a reason code. This appears procedurally adequate per CHSC § 1374.31(b).

2.  **Assessment of C5-C6 Level:**
    *   **2.1 DIAGNOSIS REQUIREMENT:** Met. The MRI shows a large disc herniation with moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression, and the neurological exam documents right C6 weakness, absent reflex, and dermatomal numbness/tingling, consistent with cervical radiculopathy (2.1a) and objective neurological deficit (2.1c).
    *   **2.2 CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT REQUIREMENT:** Met for radiculopathy.
        *   **Physical Therapy (2.2a):** 8 weeks of PT completed exceeds the 6-week minimum. C6 symptoms persisted.
        *   **Pharmacotherapy (2.2b):** Two agents (Pregabalin, Naproxen) used for >4 weeks each.
        *   **Interventional (2.2c):** A right C6 epidural steroid injection was performed.
    *   **2.3 IMAGING REQUIREMENT:** Met. MRI shows pathology at C5-C6 consistent with symptoms.
    *   **Myelopathy Exception (2.2A):** Not applicable, as this is a radiculopathy case, not primary myelopathy.

    **Conclusion for C5-C6:** This level clearly meets HealthFirst's medical necessity criteria for surgical intervention.

3.  **Assessment of C6-C7 Level:**
    *   **2.1 DIAGNOSIS REQUIREMENT:** **NOT MET.**
        *   The MRI explicitly states "no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact." This fails to demonstrate structural pathology consistent with radiculopathy (2.1a) or myelopathy (2.1b).
        *   The neurological exam showed "No definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms" and only "right tricep reflex slightly diminished," which does not constitute an "objective neurological deficit" clearly attributable to C7 compression (2.1c) given the imaging findings. Physician notes regarding C7 symptoms are qualified as "mild" and "possibly present but not clearly documented."
    *   **2.2 CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT REQUIREMENT:** Although PT was completed for 8 weeks and pharmacotherapy met, the interventional treatment was C6-specific. More importantly, the *primary failure* for C6-C7 is the lack of objective diagnosis and imaging findings, not a failure of conservative treatment trials.
    *   **2.3 IMAGING REQUIREMENT:** **NOT MET.** The MRI does not demonstrate structural pathology (nerve root compression or cord contact) at C6-C7 consistent with surgical indication.

    **Conclusion for C6-C7:** This level does **not** meet HealthFirst's medical necessity criteria for surgical intervention due to lack of objective evidence of nerve root compression or definitive neurological deficit.

---

**V. APPLICATION OF CALIFORNIA REGULATORY FRAMEWORK**

1.  **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy Prerequisite):**
    *   This provision prevents plans from requiring PT where it's contraindicated, a functional plateau is reached, or objective structural neurological compromise exists that PT cannot address.
    *   In this case, 8 weeks of PT was completed, exceeding the plan's 6-week minimum. For C5-C6, the symptoms persisted, suggesting a functional plateau was reached for that specific radiculopathy. For C6-C7, symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving," suggesting PT was either effective or the symptoms were not significant. This regulation does not override the denial for C6-C7 because the denial is based on a lack of objective pathology, not a failure to complete conservative treatment for that level. No objective structural neurological compromise is identified for C6-C7.

2.  **DMHC APL 22-014 (Myelopathy and Urgent Conditions):**
    *   This APL specifically addresses myelopathy cases and allows for waiver of conservative treatment requirements for time-sensitive neurological conditions with progressive pathology like myelomalacia.
    *   **This APL is NOT APPLICABLE** as the member's clinical record does not provide any objective evidence of cervical myelopathy or myelomalacia. This case is clearly a radiculopathy presentation.

3.  **CHSC § 1374.32(b) (IMR Standard is NOT Plan Criteria):**
    *   This critical provision mandates that services meeting "generally accepted standards of medical practice" SHALL be approved regardless of more restrictive plan criteria. Therefore, I must evaluate the request against clinical standards.

---

**VI. APPLICATION OF CLINICAL STANDARD KNOWLEDGE (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021)**

1.  **Distinction: Myelopathy vs. Radiculopathy:** The clinical standards emphasize the fundamental difference. This case is definitively a radiculopathy at C5-C6, with no evidence of myelopathy at either level.

2.  **Conservative Treatment for Radiculopathy:** For radiculopathy, 6-12 weeks of conservative treatment (PT, pharmacotherapy, injections) is generally recommended before surgery (NASS 2020). Mr. Patel completed 8 weeks of PT, 3-4 months of pharmacotherapy, and a C6-specific epidural injection. This largely aligns with standard conservative treatment recommendations for radiculopathy.

3.  **Surgical Indications for ACDF (AANS/CNS 2023):**
    *   **C5-C6 Level:** Meets TIER 2 — REASONABLE INDICATION (3.1(b)): "Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx" and 3.1(c) "Significant functional impairment not responding to conservative care." The objective neurological deficit (weakness, absent reflex) and persistent symptoms after adequate conservative treatment clearly support surgical intervention at C5-C6.
    *   **C6-C7 Level:** Falls under TIER 3 — SURGERY NOT INDICATED (3.1(b)): "Imaging findings without correlating symptoms." The MRI shows "no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact" at C6-C7, and the clinical exam shows "No definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms." Clinical standards do not support surgical intervention for mild imaging changes without clear correlating objective symptoms and nerve root compression.
    *   **Argument for simultaneous treatment of adjacent levels:** While sometimes considered, the clinical standard does not support prophylactic fusion of an asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic level lacking objective pathology (e.g., nerve root compression or myelopathy) simply because it is adjacent to a symptomatic level. The risk of future degeneration in an asymptomatic level does not outweigh the immediate surgical risks without a clear medical necessity.

---

**VII. CONFLICT RESOLUTION AND FINAL DETERMINATION**

1.  **C5-C6 Level:** Both HealthFirst Plan Criteria and generally accepted Clinical Standards concur that the C5-C6 level meets medical necessity for ACDF due to objective C6 radiculopathy and failure of conservative treatment. No state law overrides this finding.

2.  **C6-C7 Level:** Both HealthFirst Plan Criteria and generally accepted Clinical Standards concur that the C6-C7 level does **not** meet medical necessity for ACDF.
    *   **Plan Criteria:** Fails sections 2.1 (Diagnosis) and 2.3 (Imaging) due to lack of objective nerve root compression or definitive C7 radicular symptoms.
    *   **Clinical Standards:** Falls under AANS/CNS Tier 3(b) (Imaging findings without correlating symptoms). There is no high-quality evidence or guideline supporting fusion of a cervical level with "no nerve root compression identifiable" and "no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms."
    *   **State Law:** No California state law or regulatory guidance overrides the need for objective clinical and imaging evidence of pathology to justify spinal surgery, particularly for radiculopathy where myelopathy is not present.

3.  **Two-Level Request:** The original denial correctly stated that a "Two-level fusion not approved when one level meets criteria and one does not." Since C6-C7 does not meet medical necessity for fusion under any applicable standard (State Law, Clinical Standard, or Plan Criteria), the request for a *two-level* ACDF, as submitted, cannot be approved.

**DISPOSITION: UPHELD**

**WARRANT:** The denial of the two-level ACDF (C5-C6 and C6-C7) is upheld because the C6-C7 level does not demonstrate medical necessity for surgical intervention. The clinical record, including MRI findings ("no nerve root compression identifiable, no cord contact") and neurological examination ("No definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms"), fails to meet the diagnostic and imaging requirements of both HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Sections 2.1 and 2.3) and generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023, Tier 3(b)). While the C5-C6 level clearly meets criteria for ACDF, the absence of medical necessity for the C6-C7 level prevents approval of the requested two-level procedure. The arguments regarding simultaneous adjacent level treatment are not supported by evidence for asymptomatic or non-radiculopathic levels.

---

**Next Steps:** Mr. Patel's treating physician may submit a new prior authorization request for a single-level ACDF at C5-C6, which appears to meet all medical necessity criteria.

# FORMAL APPEAL DETERMINATION

**CASE PROFILE**
*   **Case ID:** PA-2024-E001
*   **Member:** Victor Patel (ID: M-667799)
*   **Age:** 60 | **State of Residence:** California
*   **Health Plan:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
*   **Coverage Effective Date:** 2016-05-01
*   **Requested Procedure:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF), C5-C6 and C6-C7 (Two-Level; CPT 22551 + CPT 22552)
*   **Requesting Physician:** Dr. Lisa Park, MD — Spine Surgery
*   **Facility:** UCSF Medical Center
*   **Date of Appeal:** November 15, 2024

---

### **FINAL DISPOSITION**
**PARTIALLY OVERTURNED**
*   **CPT 22551 (Single-level ACDF, C5-C6):** **OVERTURNED** (Approved as medically necessary).
*   **CPT 22552 (Additional level ACDF, C6-C7):** **UPHELD** (Denial affirmed; not medically necessary).

---

### **AUTHORITY & GOVERNING HIERARCHY**
This determination is issued pursuant to California regulatory standards and clinical practice guidelines. In accordance with California statutory requirements, conflict resolution is governed by the following Hierarchy of Authority: 
**California State Law (CIC / CHSC / DMHC Regulations) > Generally Accepted Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS, AO Spine, NASS) > Plan Coverage Criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024).**

---

### **DETAILED EVALUATION FINDINGS**

#### **Step 1: Procedural Adequacy and Disclosure Audit**
A review of the initial denial notice dated November 1, 2024, was conducted to ensure compliance with **California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b)**.
*   **Findings:** The denial notice issued by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD, cited the specific plan clinical coverage criteria applied (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024, Code MED-003) and provided a clear, individualized clinical explanation detailing why the C6-C7 level was excluded while acknowledging that the C5-C6 level met clinical requirements. The standard notification regarding the member's right to an Independent Medical Review (IMR) was present.
*   **Procedural Ruling:** **Positive Finding.** The denial is procedurally sound. No procedural overturn is warranted; the case must be resolved on its clinical merits.

#### **Step 2: Diagnostic Classification and Severity Assessment**
The clinical record was evaluated to classify the primary disease process as either *cervical radiculopathy* or *cervical myelopathy*.
*   **Clinical Records Review:** 
    *   **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):** Demonstrates right bicep weakness (3+/5), an absent right bicep reflex, and right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling. The tricep reflex (C7) is noted as "slightly diminished" with "no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms."
    *   **Imaging (MRI 2024-09-15):** C5-C6 shows a large disc herniation with moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression. C6-C7 shows a small disc bulge with mild foraminal narrowing and *no* cord contact or nerve root compression.
    *   **Upper Motor Neuron (UMN) Signs:** There is no documentation of gait instability, hyperreflexia (clonus), positive Hoffman sign, or bilateral symptoms.
*   **Diagnostic Classification:** **Negative Finding for Myelopathy.** The pathology is classified as **cervical radiculopathy** (specifically, active right C6 radiculopathy). There is no objective clinical or radiological evidence of cervical myelopathy.

#### **Step 3: Level-by-Level Imaging and Clinical Correlation**
An assessment of the medical necessity for surgical intervention at each requested level was performed:

*   **C5-C6 Level (CPT 22551):**
    *   *Imaging Correlation:* The MRI dated 2024-09-15 confirms a large disc herniation causing moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression.
    *   *Clinical Correlation:* The neurological exam dated 2024-09-20 demonstrates corresponding C6 nerve root deficits (3+/5 bicep weakness, absent reflex, dermatomal numbness).
    *   *Conservative Treatment History:* The patient has completed 8 weeks (24 sessions) of supervised physical therapy targeting C6 symptoms, a 4-month trial of Pregabalin (150mg BID), a 3-month trial of Naproxen (500mg BID), and a right C6 epidural steroid injection on 2024-10-15 (which yielded 70% temporary relief).
    *   *Ruling:* **Positive Finding.** The C5-C6 level meets all plan criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2) and clinical standard benchmarks for single-level ACDF.

*   **C6-C7 Level (CPT 22552):**
    *   *Imaging Correlation:* The MRI dated 2024-09-15 shows only a small disc bulge and mild foraminal narrowing with **no identifiable nerve root compression and no cord contact**.
    *   *Clinical Correlation:* The physical exam notes "no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms." The physical therapy discharge note at week 8 indicates that C7 symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving."
    *   *Conservative Treatment History:* No C7-specific interventional therapy was performed.
    *   *Ruling:* **Negative Finding.** There is no objective radiological pathology or correlating clinical deficit to support surgical decompression or fusion at C6-C7.

#### **Step 4: Statutory Override and Conservative Treatment Waiver Analysis**
We analyzed the application of **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5** and **DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014** regarding conservative treatment waivers.
*   **Findings:** Because the patient does not have cervical myelopathy, myelomalacia (T2 cord signal change), or progressive structural cord injury, the statutory provisions that mandate a waiver of conservative trials do not apply. 
*   **Standard Compliance:** The patient *has* completed the plan's standard conservative treatment requirements (exceeding 6 weeks of PT, 2 pharmacotherapy agents, and 1 injection). While this authorizes surgery for the symptomatic C5-C6 level, it does not justify surgical intervention at the asymptomatic and radiographically mild C6-C7 level.

#### **Step 5: Application of IMR Medical Necessity Standard vs. Plan Criteria**
Under **CHSC § 1374.32(b)**, the IMR medical necessity standard overrides plan-specific guidelines if the service meets generally accepted clinical standards. We evaluated the provider's appeal arguments against clinical guidelines from the **AANS/CNS (2023)** and **NASS (2020)**.
*   **Provider Argument 1:** *"Adjacent levels should be addressed simultaneously to prevent accelerated degeneration."*
    *   *Clinical Standard Evaluation:* Generally accepted clinical standards (NASS, AANS/CNS) do not support the prophylactic fusion of adjacent, non-pathological, or minimally degenerated levels. Fusing a level with only mild, asymptomatic changes (C6-C7) does not prevent adjacent segment disease; rather, it increases the biomechanical stress on the remaining mobile segments (C7-T1) and unnecessarily increases surgical morbidity.
*   **Provider Argument 2:** *"Both levels are symptomatic per treating physician."*
    *   *Clinical Standard Evaluation:* This assertion is directly contradicted by the clinical record. The physical therapy notes explicitly document that C7 symptoms were minimal and resolving by week 8, and the neurological exam states that C7 dermatomal symptoms are not clearly documented or present.
*   **IMR Medical Necessity Determination:** 
    *   **C5-C6 ACDF (CPT 22551):** Medically necessary. Satisfies AANS/CNS Tier 2 indications for persistent radiculopathy failing conservative management.
    *   **C6-C7 ACDF (CPT 22552):** Not medically necessary. Falls under Tier 3 (imaging findings without correlating symptoms), which is a clear contraindication to surgery.

---

### **DISPOSITION DIRECTIVE**

Pursuant to the **Disposition Decision Tree (Rule 3)**:
The plan’s denial is **PARTIALLY OVERTURNED**. 

1.  **ACDF C5-C6 (CPT 22551)** is **APPROVED** as medically necessary. The plan shall issue an immediate authorization for single-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at the C5-C6 level.
2.  **ACDF C6-C7 (CPT 22552 - Additional Level)** is **DENIED**. The plan's denial of the additional level is **UPHELD**, as it does not meet the medical necessity standards set forth in CHSC § 1374.32 or generally accepted spinal surgery guidelines.

REQUESTED PROCEDURE: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6, One Level (CPT 22551)
REQUESTING PROVIDER: Dr. Sarah Kim, MD — Spine Surgery
FACILITY: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
INITIAL DENIAL DATE: November 8, 2024
INITIAL REVIEWER: Dr. Patricia Huang, MD
APPEAL FILING DATE: November 22, 2024

DETERMINATION: OVERTURNED IN FULL

Dear Mr. Green and Dr. Kim,

HealthFirst Health Plan has completed its review of the first-level administrative and clinical appeal submitted on November 22, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for a single-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 (CPT code 22551) at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. 

After a comprehensive review of the clinical record, the plan's internal coverage criteria, California statutory requirements, and generally accepted standards of medical practice, the initial decision to deny coverage has been OVERTURNED IN FULL. Prior authorization is hereby APPROVED for the requested procedure.

Below is the detailed clinical and legal rationale supporting this determination.

---

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The initial denial issued on November 8, 2024, cited reason code MED-003, stating that the member did not meet the criteria for the requested procedure under plan policy. However, a detailed review of the clinical record demonstrates that the member fully satisfied all clinical criteria under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 at the time of the initial request. Furthermore, the initial denial notice was procedurally defective under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31 because it failed to attach the referenced criteria document and failed to include the mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice. Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, the plan is also prohibited from mechanically enforcing physical therapy duration requirements when a functional plateau has been documented. Therefore, on both clinical and procedural grounds, the denial must be overturned.

---

II. CLINICAL FINDINGS & PLAN CRITERIA ANALYSIS
Under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 (Effective January 1, 2024), Section 2 outlines the medical necessity criteria for cervical spinal surgery (CPT 22551). The member's clinical record satisfies every requirement:

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1):
   - Criteria: The member must have a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy (nerve root compression with radicular pain, numbness, or weakness in a dermatomal distribution) or cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit, supported by an MRI within 6 months demonstrating consistent structural pathology.
   - Clinical Evidence: The clinical record documents a presenting diagnosis of "Cervical radiculopathy C5-C6 with functional impairment." An MRI dated September 20, 2024 (within 6 months of the request) demonstrates a "C5-C6 large disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression." A neurological examination on September 25, 2024, confirms "Left C6 dermatomal numbness, bicep reflex diminished left, bicep weakness 4/5 left." This objective clinical presentation directly correlates with the C5-C6 structural pathology, fully satisfying Section 2.1(a) and (c).

2. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):
   - Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): The criteria require a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy directed toward the cervical condition. The clinical record documents that the member completed 7 weeks (total of 21 sessions) of supervised physical therapy, with notes documenting a functional plateau at week 6 and persistent radicular symptoms. This satisfies Section 2.2(a).
   - Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): The criteria require a trial of at least two approved drug classes (including NSAIDs and neuropathic agents) for a minimum of 4 weeks each. The clinical record documents that the member trialed Gabapentin 600mg TID (neuropathic agent) for 4 months with only partial relief, and Naproxen 500mg BID (NSAID) for 3 months with inadequate response. This satisfies Section 2.2(b).
   - Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): The criteria require at least one interventional treatment, such as a cervical epidural steroid injection. The clinical record documents that the member underwent a left C6 epidural steroid injection on October 28, 2024, which provided 40% temporary relief before symptoms returned to baseline within 3 weeks. This satisfies Section 2.2(c).

3. Imaging Requirement (Section 2.3):
   - Criteria: Current imaging within 6 months must demonstrate structural pathology consistent with symptoms and the proposed surgical level.
   - Clinical Evidence: The MRI from September 20, 2024, confirms a large disc herniation at C5-C6 with moderate left C6 nerve root compression, which directly matches the left C6 dermatomal numbness, diminished left bicep reflex, and left bicep weakness documented in the neurological exam. This satisfies Section 2.3.

4. Physician Documentation (Section 2.4):
   - Clinical Evidence: Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, provided the necessary clinical documentation, including the conservative treatment history, clinical rationale for surgical intervention, description of functional limitations, and discussion of surgical risks and alternatives. This satisfies Section 2.4.

Because the member met all plan criteria at the time of the initial review, the initial denial under MED-003 was clinically incorrect.

---

III. REGULATORY COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS
Under the California Regulatory Framework, the initial denial committed critical procedural violations that independently warrant an overturn:

1. Defective Denial Notice (CHSC § 1374.31):
   - Under CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2), a plan must include the specific criteria applied, the specific clinical reason for the denial, and notice of IMR rights in its written denial.
   - The initial denial notice dated November 8, 2024, referenced an attached criteria document but failed to include it. Furthermore, the plan failed to include the mandatory IMR notice.
   - Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason is legally DEFECTIVE and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines. The failure to provide the referenced criteria document and the IMR notice constitutes a clear statutory violation.

2. Physical Therapy Mandate Restrictions (CIC § 10169.5):
   - Under CIC § 10169.5(a)(2), a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy where the member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms.
   - Under CIC § 10169.5(c), a plan's internal requirement for a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy shall not be applied mechanically without reference to whether the member has achieved a functional plateau.
   - The member's physical therapy records explicitly document a functional plateau at week 6. Therefore, any mechanical application of plan criteria to deny coverage based on physical therapy duration or outcomes is prohibited under California law.

---

IV. CLINICAL EVIDENCE & MEDICAL NECESSITY ANALYSIS
Generally accepted standards of medical practice strongly support the medical necessity of the requested ACDF procedure:

1. Surgical Indications (AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023 & NASS Guidelines 2020):
   - Under the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) and NASS Guidelines (2020), surgical decompression via ACDF (CPT 22551) is indicated for patients presenting with cervical radiculopathy, objective neurological deficits (such as bicep weakness 4/5 and diminished bicep reflex), and persistent functional impairment that has failed to respond to 6 to 12 weeks of comprehensive conservative management (Tier 2 - Reasonable Indication).
   - The member has persistent radicular symptoms and objective motor weakness (4/5 bicep strength) despite completing 7 weeks of physical therapy, 4 months of neuropathic pharmacotherapy, 3 months of NSAID therapy, and a targeted epidural steroid injection. Delaying surgical intervention in a patient with objective, progressive motor weakness and a documented functional plateau is clinically contraindicated and increases the risk of permanent neurological deficit.

---

V. RESOLUTION OF CROSS-SOURCE CONFLICTS
In accordance with standard utilization review hierarchy, California State Law and generally accepted clinical standards supersede restrictive or mechanically applied plan criteria:
1. Hierarchy of Authority: California State Law (CHSC and CIC) > Generally Accepted Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS and NASS Guidelines) > HealthFirst Internal Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024).
2. Conflict Resolution: While the member fully satisfies the plan's internal criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), any interpretation by the initial reviewer suggesting that the member's conservative treatment was insufficient is directly overridden by CIC § 10169.5 (which protects members who have reached a functional plateau in physical therapy) and CHSC § 1374.32(b) (which mandates that medical necessity determinations be based on clinical appropriateness and generally accepted standards of practice rather than sole reliance on restrictive internal plan criteria).

---

VI. CONCLUSION & AUTHORIZATION DETAILS
Based on the clinical evidence demonstrating full compliance with HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, the statutory protections under California law (CHSC § 1374.31 and CIC § 10169.5), and the clinical recommendations of the AANS/CNS and NASS guidelines, the prior authorization denial is OVERTURNED.
